findings.title: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException when V2 permissions are enabled
findings.body: The new ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (line 193 of that file) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener runs on every client removal, so deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled fails or leaves the deletion half-done. The listener needs a V2-safe path (skip or implement cleanup for V2) before merge.

findings.title: Role and group removal listeners are now gated behind an unrelated feature flag
findings.body: The whole listener body was wrapped in an ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ check. Previously the RoleRemovedEvent and GroupRemovedEvent handling ran unconditionally. The PR description says nothing about this change, and it alters cleanup behavior for roles and groups in any realm where the v1 flag is off. Either justify it or keep the original unconditional behavior for the existing branches.

findings.title: NullPointerException when the 'Clients' resource-type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which returns null when the resource is absent. The next line then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null), which will likely NPE. Realms whose resource server was initialized before this PR do not have the new 'Clients' resource, so any client-permission check in those realms can fail with an NPE instead of returning false. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: Existing realms lack the new Clients type and scopes; no migration is provided
findings.body: init() only creates the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite scopes for newly created realms. For realms created before this change, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws 'No scopes found.' when a Clients permission is created, and hasPermission finds no Clients resource at all. No upgrade path or migration is included, so these realms silently get no client permissions or fail on use.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases USERS and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Clients resources are created with the internal client UUID as name and no display name, so a client-scope permission lookup may return null or an opaque UUID for display. The Clients type should be mapped to the clientId, analogous to the user username lookup.

findings.title: requireView() javadoc says it returns a boolean
findings.body: The javadoc for requireView() reads 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when the check fails. The same wrong wording appears on requireViewClientScopes(). Both should say 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false'.
